description.narrative: Development of municipal planning and local self government in Northern Kosovo. The effort consists of support for the development of municipal planning and local administration in seven municipalities in Northern Kosovo. UN-Habitat is Sida's contracting party, and will in turn work with and through local and national authorities as well as a network of civil society organizations. The overall purpose of the effort is to strengthen the ability of participating municipalities to deliver community services in accordance with Kosovo's legislation in the area, through inclusive planning. The effort also includes two smaller funds, one to support smaller municipal investments and one to support civil society organizations to strengthen them in dialogue with authorities, to demand responsibility and to represent citizens. The effort has a clear environmental perspective and an integrated conflict perspective.

Insatsen utgörs av stöd till utveckling av kommunal planering och lokal förvaltning i sju kommuner i Norra Kosovo. UN-Habitat är Sidas avtalspart, och kommer i sin tur att arbeta med och genom lokala och nationella myndigheter samt ett nätverk av civilsamhällsorganisationer. Det övergripande syftet med insatsen är att stärka medverkande kommuners förmåga att i leverera samhällstjänster i enlighet med kosovarsk lagstiftning på området, genom inklusiv planering. Insatsen omfattar även två mindre fonder, en för stöd till mindre kommunala investeringar och en för stöd till civilsamhällsorganisationer för att stärka dem i dialog med myndigheter, för att utkräva ansvar och representera medborgana. Insatsen har ett tydligt miljöperspektiv och ett integrerat konfliktperspektiv.

The overarching objective of the programme is to: Foster inclusive development and good governance in northern Kosovo through support to integration in Kosovos planning framework, with strong democratic oversight, local-central dialogue, and inter-municipal cooperation.
The programme will contribute to achievement of the headline goal through the realization of three intended outcomes:
(1) Increased integration of northern municipalities within Kosovos governance framework, achieved through development of institutional capacities to progressively improve performance of their responsibilities related to integrated spatial and urban planning and development, consistent with Kosovos planning system and principles of sound public administration
(2) Enhanced quality of local governance, achieved through extensive public dialogue, feedback and accountability mechanisms, and civil society action to demand greater municipal responsiveness and performance
(3) Strengthened public confidence in local institutions and the integration process, achieved through demonstration of practical infrastructure and service delivery improvements, and delivered by enhanced mechanisms for local-central and inter-municipal trust-building, dialogue, and coordination
The objectives of the programme, aligned with the intended outcomes above, are as follows:
(1) Facilitate alignment of northern Kosovo municipalities with the Kosovo-wide planning framework, establishing strategic planning schemes in line with Kosovos legal requirements and principles of sound public administration
(2) Increase local government transparency, responsiveness and accountability through civil society mobilization and citizen participation
(3) Foster integration by nurturing local-central and inter-municipal dialogue and cooperation, and demonstrating tangible progress to citizens by investing strategically in practical infrastructure and service delivery improvements.
The main direct beneficiaries of the Inclusive Development Programme includes:
a) Local governments. The programme provides guidance to 7 local governments in northern Kosovo, serving as a basis for policymakers to develop and refine policies and programmes that advance inclusive development and good governance. Local governments in northern Kosovo are equipped and empowered to design and implement MDPs and MZMs in line with Kosovo legal requirements, and strengthen the democratic engagement of citizens in decision-making. Support is provided to local governments to engage in local-central and inter-municipal trust-building and coordination activities, enabling them to develop practical joint projects and advocacy initiatives, to mutual advantage and satisfying citizen demands. Vitally, the programme will in the future provide municipalities with access to catalytic co-financing for infrastructure and service delivery improvements.
b) Civil society. Local CSOs benefit from opportunities to build their internal organizational and technical capacities and strengthen links with the broader public, as well as to engage directly with municipal decision-makers, contribute to formulation of strategic public responses to key issues, representing an important step toward raising the collective voice of civil society in the 7 municipalities. The programme provides CSOs with access to catalytic co-financing for actions promoting citizen participation and accountability in local governance.
c) Government of Kosovo. Central line ministries, especially MESP and MLGA currently benefit from a neutral institutional bridge to local governments in northern Kosovo, enabling them to build trust and pursue deeper engagement and alignment. More generally, the Government of Kosovo benefits from support in implementation of key aspects of Pristina-Belgrade dialogue and subsequent agreements; and are supported to develop future-oriented local government policies that leverage the advantages of subsidiarity and decentralization.
Main indirect beneficiaries of the Inclusive Development Programme will include:
Population of northern Kosovo. By investing strategically in infrastructure and service delivery improvements, the programme will contribute to tangible positive changes in living conditions in the short-term; by enhancing the effectiveness of municipal planning in 7 northern municipalities, the programme is associated with better prospects for inclusive development and stability in the long-term. The programme aims to equip citizens with new tools and resources to articulate their needs and aspirations and demand responsiveness and accountability from local institutions. The impact of programme activities is likely to be especially significant for the most vulnerable constituencies, including women, young people, and displaced persons, who are often marginalized from decision-making and sharing in the benefits of development, but who are specifically targeted during programme implementation.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The Inclusive Development Program started 2017 and its activities ended in April 2024 after several amendments to the agreement. The last additional budget was in March 2022 (see above) when the program added a component called the Green Corridor. This was a contribution to the European mobile biennial Manifesta where the municipality of Pristina and UN-Habitat worked worked closely with Manifesta team, with support also from the Embassy of Sweden. It was assessed to have relevance to the program as it involved vulnerable citizens in Pristina, in need of a better environment in their neighborhood that also would benefit many people walking in the city. However, this specific component - constructing a green path for walk parallel to the old railway track - was not as successful when it came to sustainability due to lack of maintenance of the path - its trees and benches among others.
Except from the Green Corridor, and some other new activities that were added adaptively in the time ofbig political constraints in the north, the planned goals and outcomes have been easy to follow during the years linked to framework that was planned from the beginning. Sida assesses that UN-Habitat has delivered clear reports, following the result framework and with concrete examples of results. Field trips have been possible almost the whole period, except from after the The Banjska attack in September 2023 when a armed assault carried out by Serb militants against the Kosovo Police in the northern village - affecting the work and changing the whole scenario for finalizing the program. At this time the program activities were reaching its end, related to the result framework, and many goals achieved. However, there were some last approvals and implementation missing, which also caused a prolongation of the activity period.
Following are some results linked to the three outcomes:
1) Increased integration of northern municipalities within Kosovos governance framework.
Under this outcome three different concrete outputs in line with the Kosovo law have been set, mainly for drafting, conducting and approving the important city-planning documents: Municipal Development Plans (MDP) and Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans (SUMPS). These plans have all been conducted and finalized with an inclusive process for the whole period. When it comes to the MDP:s the final approval is missing in four assemblies in the municipals Zubin Potok, Leposoviq, Zvecan, and Mitrovica North which has to do with the political instability and changes in leadership in these four municipalities. The municipalities claimed a year ago that there should be some flexibilities in the Municipal Development Plan so that they could be changed if needed. However, that is not according to the national law which points out that the plan should not be changed just because a new mayor in place. There is still - writing this memo - an ongoing dialogue between the government, UN-Habitat and these municipalities. When it comes to the SUMPS all the seven assemblies have finalized and approved them, and they are in line with EU guidelines and Kosovo law (the plans stresses the mobility such as transports, walking possibilities and cycling).
Additionally all the municipalities have conducted Municipal Citizen Participation Plans and overall guidelines for how to include citizens and make them part of the planning which is linked to the goal. All have been finalized and approved.
Under this outcome trainings and administrative support was included. The training on how to perform and evaluate Municipal Development Plans and Strategic Environmental Assessments was directed to officials from northern municipalities. This effort successfully built and strengthened the institutional capacities of around 111 central and local officials.
Besides these document the team worked with Gender analysis in all seven municipalities, and environmental assessment strategies for Vushtrri and Skenderaj. In these two mentioned municipalities specific technical assistance were also given for drafting of Municipal Zoning Map - which for example included a concept for the historic center of Vushtrri - in order to renovate and protect historical houses and paths in certain zones. These plans are being implemented now (after the activity period). Vuchtrri's historical centre - its baseline facts and assessments - are being used as a good example on how to integrate environmental, gender- and cultural heritage components into an area of a city - involving its citizen to take part of the improvements.
Another important activity when it comes to improving the living conditions for people living in areas with poor road and technical infrastructure with no access to social facilities and services, no vibrant public life, was to developing the neighborhood based planning. The selected sites for analysis encompassed several urban and rural neighborhoods around the Ibar River and the Artificial Lake, such as the Center Fidanishte, Roma Mahalla, Ilirida and Zhabar i Peshtëm. The municipality of Skederaj selected Runik as a district of strategic importance for municipality's and the whole region's development due to its richness with natural and cultural heritage and multi-ethnic communities.
2) Enhanced quality of local governance, achieved through extensive public dialogue, feedback and accountability mechanisms, and civil society action to demand greater municipal responsiveness and performance.
Under this outcome Civil society has been strengthened to for example advocate for local government transparency. A specific catalytic fund was formed - The Civil Society Catalytic Fund (CSCF) - with Calls for Proposals for innovative projects that encouraged civil society to take part of local policy making processes and strengthen their own capacity to reach out to citizens, the municipalities and government.
One of the results from this was that the coordination among the organizations improved and CBM, Community Building Mitrovica, enhanced its capacity as a sort of umbrella organization for NGO:s in northern Kosovo. This improvement of capacity, staff and routines made the Inclusive Development Program stronger - bridging the civil society to the municipalities. Parallel to the capacity development of civil society coordination, around 35 new initiatives were started. These initiative gathered and organized groups that was not formally organized, like elderly, persons with disability and young people - all with different backgrounds and ethnicity. Four municipalities were engaged; Leposavic, Zubin Potok, Mitrovica North and Zvecan. Except from gathering for a stronger voice, the organizations produced hand crafts, music, food. The goal, to stimulate civil society action, contributing to a more participatory and responsive governance framework in northern Kosovo, was assessed by the team to have been reached and satisfactory.
Another project under the catalytic fund was a public opinion research on youth entrepreneurship with 60% of the respondents being Kosovo Albanians, a third were Kosovo Serbs, and a bit over 5 percent were Bosniaks. The survey was done by NGO LINK with 400 respondents, in 2019. The report showed what kind of support the youth would like to see to start a business or get a job. Over 60 percent thought that the municipality should provide subsidies for start-ups and 45 percent thought that the municipalities should better promote local businesses and se the potentials. More than 70 percent of the respondents would like to be a part of a working group for the development of the municipal strategy for youth entrepreneurship.
Generally speaking the survey showed that the transparency of the municipalities was perceived as poor, and this was something that the Inclusive Development Program took into account when planning the activities ahead.
Finally, under this outcome, important to mention is the Capital Investments project proposals. Parallel to supporting civil society to engage in policy making and a like, support was given to the municipalities to plan for infrastructure project needed to improve the conditions in the city- or urban area. These proposals were implemented under the outcome 3 - with financial support from the Local Government Administration and Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure Ministry, in November 2021. Within the Inclusive Development Program the Capital Investment Facility, CIF, had been going on since 2020 (in the first year this initiative was called capital investments projects, CIP and it was only directed to the seven municipalities). In 2021 the Facility reached out to all the municipalities in Kosovo. At the same this time the Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports, pitched in financial support to the program to improve the integration of the cultural heritage sites in the city planning with extra expertise from the ministry.
3) Strengthened public confidence in local institutions and the integration process.
As mentioned above; the implementation of the Capital Investment Facility targeted seven municipalities in the north in the first year, and then all Kosovo 38 municipalities. After a process of assessments of the plans, different investments were implemented and they were resulting in concrete project. For the seven municipalities, the following examples of infrastructure projects were implemented during 2021 and 2022:
- A reconstruction and adaptation of a production hall for the Fire Unit's need in Zvecan. - A historic path with renovated houses in Vushtrri. - A facility and public space in Leposavic for civil society organizations - especially young persons for different activities, including environmental actions. - A broad and accessible friendly walk "Enjoy the Town on Foot" in Skenderaj. - An enhanced market capacity for trade among the municipalities in Zubin Potok. - A public space and paths along the Ibar River and Artificial Lake in Mitrovica South. - A reconstruction of the road in the city center between two roundabouts with extra space for children's playground in Mitrovica North.
The implementation of the Capital Investment Facility has been summarized and analyzed from a regional comparative perspective, and by including other grants given to the municipalities, in the whole country. The result shows differences and similarities regarding the priorities in the municipalities. Mostly the priorities have been infrastructure projects like improvement of roads and bridges and some central municipality houses. The obvious priorities from the municipalities have caused debates at regional meetings and workshops which became a collaboration between the municipalities, UN-Habitat, the above ministries and the Ministry for regional development - upon request from the municipalities in the north. During these meetings questions who decided the priorities when applying for the grants were discussed. It became clear that there was a gap in planning when it comes to involving both men and women. The requests and expressed needs from women were more seldom taken into account. This was for example lifted by women from the northern municipalities who stressed that they need more focus on buildings and teachers for children care, so that women in especially the rural areas can start working. Regarding plans for school, social services and transports it become clear that a better cooperation between the regions are needed.
Generally the third outcome, where the implementation of CIF and other activities are structured, has been integrated in all the work under the two other outcomes. The methodology linked to inclusiveness that UN-Habitat has used is based on practical actions like meetings, workshops with in depth facilitation and networking. It also includes reach-out activities to involve as many civil servants, city planners, organizations, private sector and citizens as possible with whom the team has had pre meetings for analysis of the current situation to see what needs to be improved or developed. The above workshops with the regional perspectives were for instance hold for the first time in Kosovo. Unfortunately the northern municipalities who explicitly had wanted the gathering couldn't join the last meetings due to severe political situation and escalating conflict in the north.
A special activity under this outcome involved all the Directors of the Collegia for Spatial Planning, under the Association of Kosovo municipalities, where various challenges were discussed and categorized and evaluated. An assessment of the Geographical Information System (GIS) was a collaborative effort involving the member municipalities of the Collegia. The findings have been documented and started a process in improving different systems for all municipalities - regarding a more efficient city- and rural planning.
Lastly to be mentioned here is the Local Climate Action Forum (LoCAF) that was initiated within the Inclusive Development program, gathering 28 organizations in Kosovo to give extra perspective on environmental issues for city- and rural planning.
Unexpected results
The regional perspective, with joint workshops involving the seven municipalities with other municipalities in Kosovo was a result of an adaptive approach in the program. The joint workshops with all the municipalities in Kosovo was not planned for in the beginning of the intervention, as the focus was merely on the north. However, an holistic approach with a system analysis was formed during the different activities in respective municipality and it was requested from the involved partners, civil society and some of the municipalities. It was also a part of a new way of working at the ministry level, aligned with the new regional strategy where regional hubs in the country are now being developed.
Some other examples:
- The Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure, MESPI requested expertise from UNHabitat in the processes of auditing and conducting a report regarding SPAK which is the Spatial Planning Application Kosovo database. The final report covered analysis and recommendations to improving and addressing gaps within the planning system in Kosovo, aligned with the Law No. 04/L174 for the management of the National Consolidated Spatial Planning Database.
Although this activity was not within the framework for IDP, the Inclusive Development program, the report served a good understanding for the needs in municipalities like Skederaj, Mitrovica South and Vushtrri who are part of the IDP. This report has been part of UNHabitat's engagement in the interministerial working group tasked with drafting the new Kosovo Spatial Plan. The Kosovo Institute for Spatial Planning will further collaboration with UN-Habitat in improving and establishing a central level database with accurate data.
- Evaluation of the governments three year Municipal Housing Programs, using criteria derived from the Municipal Housing Program conducted by UN-Habitat in Gjilan in 2014, as well as data from the OECD database. Recommendations have been given for a more cohesive Municipal Housing Programmes for a harmonized and sustainable housing strategy at national level. A draft of the law on Social Housing was produced, thanks to a support of 25 million euros from CEB, Italian Funds for Innovative Projects and a 2 million Euros grant received by the Government.
- Together with local civil society organizations from Skenderaj/Srbica, Mitrovica South, Leposaviq/Leposavic and Zubin Potok, the project "Emergency Livelihood Assistance to Floods Affected Housholds in Kosovo" was integrated in the program, and in the urban and rural planning. The activities were directly linked to the flooding and immediate needs that took place during January 2023, but also for a long term solution for overall resilience and recovery of the community affected by the floods. Around 130 households were involved, as well as researches, students, police men, civil servants working with disaster preparedness. These activities were supported by Government of Switzerland through FAO. Next step in these activities are to deliver more essential goods and services to most flood affected families for better preparation, and enhanced knowledge in the community how to be more resilience.
- An exploring meeting regarding regional development was held online, facilitated by the Embassy but within the program as there was a request by the Ministry of Regional Development to have an exchange with Sweden when it comes to different tasks, such as institutionalisations of regional hubs in Kosovo. Participants from Sweden were from Salar International, Swedish Association of Local Authorities and Region, Swedish Ministry of Rural Affairs and Infrastructure and Swedish Agency for Economi and Regional Growth. From Kosovo staff from the Embassy, UN-Habitat and the Ministry of Regional Development participated. The outcome of the meeting was that there are wishes for collaboration in the area of regional analysis (statistics and coordination), trade, transport, technical assistance for legal framework, strengthening of integrating equality and human capacities in regional coordination, and support to businesses and capital investments projects. UN-Habitat hosted a follow-up meeting conference 16-17 April 2024 which was more of a presentation of potential and existing business developing in Kosovo. No further action was taken to strengthen the collaboration between Sweden and Kosovo regarding regional development, as Sida has no resources for a contribution that would support it. Sida, however, has recommended Kosovo-actors to apply for support through Swedish Institute.
- The interest from the Ministry of Culture to improve the integration of Cultural heritage in City- and Rural planning resulted in a special focus on areas in the north with archaeological sites that can develop, and create job, in the nearby towns. The Roman urban settlement Municipium Dardanicum, near today's Soanica, was discussed as a potential focus for future remake and renovation. There is little written about this place, but data from a systematic research and investigation, carried out in the beginning of 1960, can be further utilized and the site could be better protected.
During the Inclusive development program the focus on a holistic approach to culture heritage has improved also for the village Zym, the historical centre of Pristina and further development in Prizren with restoration of an archaeological site. The Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports has after the end of the activity period of IDP asked for further cooperation to strengthen the Cultural Creative Business sector in Kosovo, putting the culture heritage into a broader picture.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
